mode: Pinned UTF-8 PostgreSQL with standard_conforming_strings on, pg_catalog first and stock native assignment casts.
structure: A native Boolean destination is an explicit typed target role. VALUES cells contain TRUE, FALSE or NULL in that position. UPDATE also accepts a resolved Boolean old-row field. INSERT SELECT accepts Boolean field reads, Boolean literals, Boolean tests, builtin Boolean casts and NULL with the target context required below.
conditions: Validate target occurrence, native type and unique writable position. The projection width and destination layout agree in order. Check each Boolean read against its own source. Reject Boolean and signed or text roles in unrelated destinations. A bare NULL resolves to Boolean in an ordinary SELECT assignment. DISTINCT resolves bare NULL to text and cannot write it to a Boolean field. A builtin Boolean cast supplies a typed NULL before DISTINCT.
meaning: Write positional truth values with the original duplicate policy, SQL NULL and target defaults on omitted fields. UPDATE computes all assigned values from the old row, then RETURNING reads the new row. Query writes retain independently scoped Boolean field reads. INSERT and UPDATE use the owning table and preserve typed output and affected rows.
sql: Render checked truth values as TRUE or FALSE and explicit NULL in VALUES or UPDATE. Render a planned query NULL or typed cast with pg_catalog.bool when required. Preserve independent source columns, DISTINCT policy and output and destination order.
observations: Exact native destination and source roles and positions
Ordered RETURNING names and type identifiers, affected row count, Boolean values and NULL
Full target row bags before, after and restored by rollback, and unchanged source rows
Native type errors for incompatible assignments and DISTINCT untyped NULL

finite.completeness: Recover row width, operation and native slot order, typed values, duplicate policy, scoped old-row reads, and filter from the constructed graph. Require exactly one result for each fixed identity.
